analysis.title: ING Groep N.V.: Mixed margin trends, shifting focus to CMD
key_insights: RBC keeps ING at Sector Perform and raises the 12-month price target to EUR34 from EUR33, rolled forward to 2028 estimates. The shares are at EUR28.85, implying 18.1% upside to the target.
The liability margin rose 6bp in Q3 to 113bp, after a 3bp rise in Q2. ING guides to 110bp for the year, which implies close to 116bp in Q4. RBC models a further rise to 120bp in 2028.

The lending margin fell 1bp in Q3 to 123bp and ING guided to an unchanged level in Q4. ING attributes the decline to its focus on higher-return lending (mortgages, investment-grade). RBC now models 126bp in 2028, down from 129bp.

RBC's Vault data shows deposit competition in the Netherlands is somewhat contained, while Germany remains competitive. ING launched a campaign in Germany offering new customers 3.5% for a limited time, still below the top rates in the market.
Q3 deposit growth was relatively strong, especially in wholesale banking (cash management and payments).
ING is restructuring wholesale banking into Corporate & Institutional Banking, with cost saves of EUR75m a year from 2028 and a EUR175m restructuring charge in Q4.

Wholesale banking ROE was 11% in Q3 2026 against the previous 2027 target of above 12%. RBC includes a 20bp benefit from significant risk transfers (SRTs) by 2028, which takes its 2028E wholesale ROE to 13%.
Each 1pt improvement in RBC's 2028E wholesale ROE would add 2% to profits and 0.4pt to group ROTE.
The Capital Markets Day on 14 June 2027 is expected to set 2030 targets and may lay out further ROE expansion. RBC sees it as potential upside to its estimates.
RBC continues to model special distributions rising to EUR4bn in 2028, supported by capital optimization.
RBC cuts EPS estimates by 3.9% for 2027 and 5.4% for 2028 (2026 is up 0.2%), mainly from the lower lending margin forecast. 2028E EPS is EUR3.28 against EUR3.46 before.
Sensitivity: a 1% change in loan/deposit volume growth is close to 1% of 2028E PBT, and a 1bp margin change moves 2028E PBT by 1%.
RBC's 2027E and 2028E reported PBT are 5% and 6% below ING-collected consensus (collected before Q3 results). DPS is 2% below consensus for both years.

market_movers.rationale: RBC raised its PT to EUR34 from EUR33 as it rolled valuation forward to 2028 estimates and kept Sector Perform. It cut EPS estimates on lower lending margins.

sector_views.rationale: ING is rated Sector Perform. Returns are expected in line with RBC's sector average over 12 months.

earnings_insights: ING Q3 2026 (reported): liability margin 113bp (+6bp q/q), lending margin 123bp (-1bp q/q).
RBC EPS, adjusted diluted: 2026E EUR2.56 (previous EUR2.55), 2027E EUR2.90 (previous EUR3.01), 2028E EUR3.28 (previous EUR3.46). 2025A was EUR2.18.
RBC adjusted ROTE estimates: 16.2% 2026E, 17.7% 2027E, 18.9% 2028E, against 14.2% in 2025A.
RBC DPS estimates (cash dividends only): EUR1.26 for 2026E, EUR1.48 for 2027E, EUR1.68 for 2028E. 2026E yield is 4.4%.
RBC net interest income estimates: EUR16,873m 2026E, EUR18,288m 2027E, EUR19,093m 2028E, against EUR14,681m in 2025A.
ING's 2026 guidance is for a 110bp liability margin. Target ROTE was raised at Q2 2026 to above 15% for 2026 and above 16% for 2027, and confirmed at Q3. Cost guidance for 2026 and 2027 is unchanged.
risk_factors: A European recession would hit earnings across ING's divisions.
ING has relatively high exposure to Russia and Ukraine-related risk.
Net interest income is a larger share of revenue at ING than at other banks (64% of group revenue in 2025), so changes in rates or volume growth move its estimates more.
ING has higher exposure to the energy sector than other banks.
Litigation risk, including the threatened 'Friends of the Earth' lawsuit in the Netherlands over ING's exposure to energy-intensive industries.
Regulatory changes to capital, funding or liquidity ratios could affect the price target.
The estimates assume buybacks. Regulatory headwinds, a higher capital requirement, a higher share price or an acquisition could reduce their benefit.
charts_described: Exhibit 5 is titled as showing that ING started new campaigns in Germany in Q4 offering a 3.5% rate.

Exhibit 7 is an NII scenario model: lending margin 126bp in Q1 2026 falling to 123bp in Q3 and Q4E, liability margin 104bp in Q1 rising to 116bp in Q4E, and total reported NII of EUR4,262m in Q3 2026 and EUR4,430m in Q4E.
geopolitical: The report lists ING's relatively high exposure to Russia and to Ukraine-related risk as a risk to its rating and price target.
The report cites current geopolitical events and a spike in energy prices, with consequences for European inflation and growth, as a risk to its estimates.
